newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria's Stoiber criticises Kinkel for EMU remark.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria's Stoiber criticises Kinkel for EMU remark.

text.p: Edmund Stoiber, premier of Germany's largest state Bavaria, has criticised Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel for saying the launch of European monetary union is already certain, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"Nobody can talk of a 'point of no return'...Whoever does that does not really take the stability criteria seriously," Stoiber told the Handelsblatt daily in a release ahead of publication on Wednesday.
Kinkel said on Monday the point of no return had been passed on the road to economic and monetary union (EMU).

Stoiber, the most prominent Eurosceptic among German conservatives, last week said adherence to EMU convergence criteria was more important than the timetable, which foresees a 1999 start for the single currency.
The Handelsblatt also quoted Finance Minister Theo Waigel as criticising Kinkel.
"I advise my colleague Kinkel and other European foreign ministers to stick to their own task of political union and spare us their advice about currency union," he said.
